newsitem.title: ITALY: BancoNapoli seeks damages from accountants.
newsitem.headline: BancoNapoli seeks damages from accountants.

text.p: Banco di Napoli said on Tuesday it was seeking damages from its previous managers as well as accountants Price Waterhouse following the discovery of hidden losses in recent years.

The board of southern Italy's largest bank said in a statement it wanted two trillion lire ($1.17 billion) from Price Waterhouse, which reviewed the bank's accounts between 1991 and 1994 and has denied any wrong-doing.

In addition, Banco di Napoli said it was looking for 1.5 trillion lire from leading managers at the bank between July 1991 to January 1995. All those concerned have been notified but the first court hearing has not yet been set.

Banco di Napoli uncovered record losses of 3.16 trillion lire in 1995 and plunged a further 1.65 trillion lire into the red last year, forcing the government to launch a rescue plan for the struggling group.

The bank's board said that the size of the damages had been based on the fact that profits were distributed in the early 1990s in the mistaken belief that the group was in the black. Taxes had also been paid on the non-existant earnings.
Price Waterhouse in Italy rejected the claims.
"We firmly deny any accusation of negligence in certifying Banco di Napoli accounts between 1986 and 1994," the firm's chairman Sergio Duca said in a statement.
"This demonstrates once again that companies in difficulty try to salvage their position by off-loading management responsiblity onto the people who check the accounts," the statement added.

The Italian Treasury installed new management at Banco di Napoli in early 1995 when the size of the losses became evident. Previously the group had been controlled by a non-profit making foundation and run more as a political fiefdom than a viable financial business.
A restructuring programme was rapidly launched, with non-core operations put up for sale and non-performing loans hived off into a separate firm underwritten by the state.
Insurer INA and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro are due to take a 60 percent stake in Banco di Napoli later this year.
